title: Papa Tio's reputation and home; Creole speech
summary: Tio was only a teacher, charged whether you came or not, lived in the Creole section; Clem's French-speaking father.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yeah, but T.O. wasn't always famous, I know.
Yeah, well, I didn't know him to play when I got acquainted with him and started. That's all he was doing, teaching. Yeah. And you'd have to pay him whether you come or not. He had that system.
You went to his home. Do you remember where he lived?

I can't remember that street so well. That's been a long time, 40, 40 times. He lived down below Dumain, the street next to Dumain Street. Yeah, they would call the name of it. What up? This is Humain and then there's St. Philip. He lived down on St. Philip and Murray, rather than that. And Robinson or Murray. Yeah. Not Robinson. Yeah. Philip, yeah.
Well, there's some of the Billary is back there and then Claver. He didn't play there.
Yeah. Well, Billary, he didn't live on Billary. He lived right next street to Dumain Street. Not just like Dumain. Yeah, probably St. Philip. Yeah. Right in that section.
Yeah, they call that the Creole section. Oh, yeah.
Did he talk Creole sometimes to you or did he usually?
No, he didn't, but I could understand a little bit because my father couldn't talk English. Was he French?
You were a French family, huh?
My father was on my mother's side. Yeah.
